name: Bajaj Auto Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest motorcycle exporter and a leading 3-wheeler maker (Pulsar, Dominar, Platina, Chetak EV, RE/Compact 3W), controlling KTM/Pierer Bajaj (BMAG), Husqvarna and the Triumph manufacturing partnership. Exports are roughly half of standalone revenue. Q2 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 20,003 cr (+34%), profit Rs 3,354 cr (+35%) on an export surge; consolidated sales Rs 25,126 cr, OPM 19%. Net cash/investment-rich. Domestic 2W weakened in September (-12%) then recovered in October; JPMorgan upgraded to Overweight and CLSA sees ~29% upside (Moneycontrol 2026-10-28).

supply_chain.note: Group NBFC financing Bajaj vehicles (model knowledge)
Step-down subsidiary; EBIT turned positive at EUR 11.3m

company_events.event: India-US trade deal or further tariff changes affecting KTM/Triumph exports

current_state.latest_quarter: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): consolidated sales Rs 25,126 cr, EBITDA Rs 4,896 cr (OPM 19%), PAT Rs 3,384 cr; standalone revenue Rs 20,003 cr (+34%), PAT Rs 3,354 cr (+35%)
current_state.trend: Export-led growth; consolidated revenue +48% TTM; margin 19-21%; interest cost rising (KTM debt) to Rs 469 cr/quarter
current_state.valuation: P/E 22.4, P/B 8.0, EV/EBITDA ~18x TTM (computed); dividend yield 1.4%; the cheapest P/E in the batch's 2W pair
recent_developments: 2026-10-01: stock -6.5% to -9% on September domestic 2W sales -12%
2026-10-27: Q2 beat, JPMorgan upgrade to Overweight, CLSA sees 29% upside
2026-11-02: two-wheeler makers post strong October sales amid cost overhang (Upstox)

key_risks: Export currency shortages in Nigeria/Egypt and volatile Africa demand
upside_triggers: Sustained export run-rate >2.5 lakh units a month

new_nodes_proposed.name: Competitive intensity in Indian two-wheelers/EV two-wheelers

exposures.mechanism: Domestic ~50% of revenue; +10% domestic industry volumes => +5% revenue; incremental margin ~35% vs 19-20% OPM => EBITDA +9%; EV/MCap ~1.0; persistence 0.5 => ~+4.4. September domestic 2W fell 12% (stock -6.5 to -9% on 2026-10-01), October recovered.

Exports ~45-50% of standalone revenue (USD/EUR/other) vs imports ~15% (KTM parts, electronics): net long ~30% of revenue; +3% => +0.9% of revenue; 80% flow-through after 12-month hedges => EBITDA +3.6%; x1.0 x0.5 => +1.8-2.0.

Steel ~15% of costs => 12% of revenue; +7% => 0.84% of revenue => EBITDA -4.2%; 60% unrecovered => -2.5%; x1.0 x0.3 => -0.7. Empirical F_STEEL_GLOBAL +1.0 (t=1.3, positive) is a cyclical co-movement and not a cost benefit.

Aluminium ~7% of costs => 5.6% of revenue; +10% => EBITDA -2.8%; 60% unrecovered => -1.7%; x0.3 => -0.5. Empirical +1.19 (t=1.5) is positive (cyclical) so range reaches +0.5. Aluminium -19.6% since June is a margin tailwind.

Empirical +1.06 (t=2.2) per +10% Brent is significant: higher oil lifts incomes in Nigeria, Angola, Colombia, Egypt and the Gulf, which buy Bajaj three-wheelers and motorcycles (exports ~half of revenue). Offset by India petrol cost and plastics (~-0.5). Net +0.8.

Africa+LatAm ~55% of exports (~25% of revenue); +1pp regional growth with export elasticity ~2 => +0.5% revenue => EBITDA +0.9% => ~+0.6. The company's weekly export run-rate (below 2.5 lakh units in Sept for the first time in four months) shows volatility.
Middle East/North Africa ~10% of exports; escalation disrupts shipping and lifts freight. -1.0 for an escalation unit (revenue -1%, EBITDA -2% x0.5).

KTM/Husqvarna/Triumph and Bajaj Auto Intl. Europe: consolidated revenue (25,126 cr) exceeds standalone (20,003 cr) by ~20%, mostly KTM/BMAG. +1pp Euro-zone growth with discretionary-motorcycle elasticity 3 => +0.6% consolidated revenue; BMAG EBIT turning positive (EUR 11.3m) => high operating leverage => +0.8.

Triumph/KTM/Husqvarna 400cc models made in India are shipped to the US; a +10pp tariff on India-origin goods is partly shared with dealers/customers. US ~4% of revenue (estimate) => EBITDA -1.5% x0.5 => -0.8. India-US talks stalled again (Reuters 2026-10-06).

P/E 22 and large investment book: valuation falls on +25bp (-1.5% DCF) but treasury income (about Rs 15,000 cr of investments, estimate) rises on higher yields => net -1.2. RBI hiked repo to 5.50% on 7 Oct; Bajaj Auto and Ashok Leyland were among top losers that day.
Chetak e-scooter and e-3W (est. 10-12% of domestic 2W revenue) benefit from stronger EV push; +1 => +1%.

Chetak motors need rare-earth magnets; a +1 tightening cut EV output in 2025 and flagged again in Aug 2026 analyst calls. EV ~10% of domestic revenue; -15% output => EBITDA -1.5% x0.7 => about -1.0; rounded -1.5.
Domestic share battle with Hero, Honda, TVS and EV start-ups. +1 => -5% domestic volume or -1% price => EBITDA -6% x0.4 => -2. Domestic 2W -12% in Sept shows share loss risk.
Pulsar, Dominar, Triumph, KTM mix lifts ASP; +1 => +1% ASP => EBITDA +5% x0.3 => +1.5.

company_links.mechanism: Bajaj Holdings owns about 5% of Bajaj Auto (~17% of its NAV, model knowledge). Unit: % change in BAJAJHLDNG equity value per +1% change in BAJAJ-AUTO equity value; 0.17 x ~0.7 after the holding-company discount behaviour = 0.12.
